v.own_numbers: Caveat: the description never defines P. From the alternating-sum structure (delta antisymmetry delta_x=-delta_{D+1-x} turns A_n into a window sum of delta over the residue class x_0 mod r) I inferred P_b = A(q)*[b]_{q^r} = A(q)(1-q^{br})/(1-q^r); every check below confirms this reading. Own exact big-integer computation (Python, prefix-sum multiplication by [a]_q): k=127, D=214497, F=0, A symmetric, delta antisymmetric. Direct unimodality of P_b for b=1..7 (two independent tests: sign pattern of (1-q)P_b, and direct monotone-up-then-down scan of P_b coefficients): b=1,2,3,5 unimodal; b=4,6,7 NOT unimodal (first violations at positions 120142, 128737, 128736). So U∩[1,7]={1,2,3,5} -- matches. Pair C=8594 (=r-1, even, == D+1 mod 2): sign(a_n) for n=0..11 = +,+,+,-,+,-,+,-,+,-,+,- so n*(C)=3; a_3+y_5>=0 (positive), a_5+y_7>=0 (positive), a_7+y_9<0, hence beta_C=7 exactly (b odd since F=0) -- matches, beta_C=7 > n*+2=5. Cross-identity: for every n=0..7, a_n equals the (1-q)P_{n+1} coefficient at position x_0+C+floor(n/2)r (n odd) / x_0+(n/2)r (n even), which lies at or before the centre, and a_{b-2}+y_b equals minus the (1-q)P_b coefficient at x_0+((b-1)/2+1)r (past centre) -- so a_n<0 and a_{b-2}+y_b<0 are genuine certificates of non-unimodality (a_3<0 is exactly the b=4 failure at 120141/120142). Scanning all 4297 class pairs of this instance: beta_C>n*+2 happens only for C=8594; n* distribution {3:699, 5:3573, 7:25}.
v.new_instances_tested: All new instances used my own ground-truth unimodality (full coefficient scan of (1-q)P_b), and for every class pair C and every b<=B checked: (i) a_n == coefficient of (1-q)P_{n+1} at the predicted position, (ii) a_{b-2}+y_b == +/- coefficient of (1-q)P_b at predicted position, (iii) a_n<0 => P_{n+1} non-unimodal and a_{b-2}+y_b<0 => P_b non-unimodal, (iv) any pair with beta_C>n*+2 re-verified from the coefficients, (v) whether every non-unimodal P_b is certified by some pair-local test. Batches: 640 small random instances (k 3-30, a_i 5-320, r 3-970, B 4-12, including F>0 cases and even r): 0 mismatches, 0 finite counterexamples, 0 uncertified non-unimodal b. 25 instances in the claimed regime (k 101-169, a_i ~1500-2200, r ~5*a_i, B=9, D up to 331k): 0 mismatches; found ONE independent new counterexample of the same shape: k=142, r=10331, C=10330=r-1, n*=3, beta=7, U∩[1,9]={1,2,3,5}, confirmed by direct coefficients. 3 'big' instances (k 172-216, a_i 1500-3000, D 338k-549k, r 2167-5062): 0 mismatches, all P_1..P_9 unimodal. 2 targeted large instances (k=200, a_i 2500-2512, r=12800, D=500924; k=180, a_i 3000-3010, r=15000, D=540807): U∩[1,9]={1..7}, 0 mismatches, 0 counterexamples. 12 F>0 instances (a_i>r, k 45-90, F 45-158, even-b beta parity): 0 mismatches. 8 even-r instances (k 72-116, r 1302-4496): 0 mismatches. Total ~690 new instances, zero mismatches anywhere.
v.reasons: Every claimed number reproduces exactly from an independent implementation: U∩[1,7]={1,2,3,5} (b=4,6,7 not unimodal, verified by two separate unimodality tests), and for C=8594: n*=3, beta_C=7 (with a_7+y_9<0, so beta is exactly 7), hence beta_C > n*+2 and the pair-local parity-gap statement fails on this instance. The internal consistency of the construction was verified (pair-local quantities are literally (1-q)P_b coefficients at specific positions, so a negative a_n / a_{b-2}+y_b is a true non-unimodality certificate), and ~690 new instances outside the claimed range (larger k up to 216, a_i up to 3010, D up to 549k, other r incl. even r, and F>0) showed zero mismatches between pair-local tests and ground-truth unimodality; one further counterexample of the identical shape (C=r-1, n*=3, beta=7) appeared in a fresh instance, so the phenomenon is reproducible and not an artifact. Caveats: (a) P was not defined in the description -- I inferred P_b=A(q)[b]_{q^r}; the exact reproduction of the nontrivial pattern {1,2,3,5} plus the coefficient identities make this inference essentially certain; (b) 'S2' is undefined, so I could only verify the stated numbers, not the meaning of 'S2 holds here'; (c) the role of F in the b-parity rule was tested only in the sense that the pair-local tests remained valid certificates for F>0 instances.

Unimodality: b=1 T, 2 T, 3 T, 4 F (peak 119442, re-ascent at 120142), 5 T, 6 F, 7 F -> U∩[1,7]={1,2,3,5}, matching CLAIM 1. Claim 2 for C=8594 (D+1 odd, C even: parity condition holds): Z=(8594,8596,25784,25786,42974,42976,60164,60166,...), x_n=(102952,102951,94357,94356,85762,85761,77167,77166,...), y_n=delta_{x_n} computed; a_0>0,a_1>0,a_2>0,a_3<0 so n*=3; a_3+y_5 = +2.08e409 >=0, a_5+y_7 = +2.45e405 >=0, a_7+y_9 = -1.5e411 <0, so beta_C=7 (and stays 7 for any cutoff >= 7), matching n*=3, beta_C=7 > n*+2=5. Cross-checks: PARI/GP independent polynomial product reproduced A's coefficients at all eight positions x_0..x_7 exactly; two different unimodality implementations agree; routines validated against sympy brute force on 200 small random (r,a,b) instances with zero disagreements.
v.new_instances_tested: (1) b=8,9,10,11,12 for the same (r,a): all NOT weakly unimodal (first violation at the same location, peak 124464 / re-ascent 128736, as for b=6,7) -> U∩[1,12]={1,2,3,5}. (2) Claim-2 procedure on other class pairs of the same instance: C=8592,8590,8580,8000 give n*=3, beta_C=5; C=2 gives n*=7, beta_C=7; C=8594 is the only one tested with beta_C=7 > n*+2. (3) 40 random small instances (r in [2,7], k<=4, a_i<=9, b<=5): coefficient and unimodality routines match sympy brute force exactly.
v.reasons: Every claimed number reproduces from an independent implementation built only from the problem statement and the claim's definitions: U∩[1,7]={1,2,3,5} (b=4,6,7 fail, b=1,2,3,5 unimodal), and for C=8594: n*(C)=3, a_3+y_5>=0 and a_5+y_7>=0 while a_3<0, so beta_C=7 (> n*+2=5). Coefficients were cross-validated with PARI/GP, the unimodality test with a second implementation, and the whole pipeline against sympy brute force on small cases. Out-of-range tests (b=8..12, other C) produced no inconsistency with the claim. No mismatch found.
